       IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
  CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Civil Appeal  No(s).  522/2017
COMMISSIONER ,COMMERCIAL TAX U.P. & ORS.          Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
GUPTA SUPPLIERS COMPANY                            Respondent(s)
     O R D E R
1. Learned counsel  for the  appellants submits
that  the  present  civil  appeal  arises  out  of  the
proceedings concerning seizure of mentha oil which was
transported from Barabanki, U. P. to Jammu and Kashmir on
23.08.2010.  The  respondent-assessee  challenged  the
seizure before the High Court and by an interim order,
the High Court released the seized goods and thereafter,
assessment proceedings have been concluded.
2. Thus, the cause of action for continuing the
present second appeal does not survive.
3. However, learned  counsel for  the appellant
submits that the High Court, under the impugned order,
has imposed cost of Rs.50,000/- on the appellants(s)
leaving it open for the appellant-State of Uttar Pradesh
to recover the cost from the pensionary benefits of the
officer or officers concerned, who were responsible for
the seizure which has been set aside by the High Court.

--- Page 248 ---
2
4. This Court has not passed any interim order
staying the imposition of cost on the appellant(s).
Therefore, in all probability, the cost imposed must have
been  deposited  by  the  appellant(s)  by  this  time.
Nevertheless,  we are of the considered view that the
direction of recovery of the cost from the pensionary
benefits of the officer or officers concerned who are
responsible for the subject seizure is neither warranted
nor correct for the reason that the officer or officers
concerned who effected the seizure, were not party to the
Writ Petition and they have never been heard before
issuing direction for the recovery of the cost from the
pensionary benefits admissible to the said officer or
officers concerned.
5. In the above view of the matter, we set aside
the said portion of the impugned order wherein, the High
Court has left it open for the State Government to
recover the cost of Rs.50,000/- from the pensionary
benefits of the officer or officers concerned who are
responsible for the impugned order of seizure.
6. The Civil Appeal stands allowed only to the
above extent without interfering with the impugned order
on merits.

--- Page 249 ---
3
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.
......................J.
   (PRASHANT KUMAR MISHRA)
....................J.
(SHREE CHANDRASHEKHAR)
New Delhi
23-07-2026

B. VINOTH KUMAR               PETITIONER/APPLICANT
                                VERSUS
V. MUTHURAMALINGAM                                    RESPONDENT
O R D E R
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The petitioner-applicant is accused in a case filed under the
Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (for short, the “N.I. Act”) by the
respondent-complainant alleging non-encashment of one post-dated
cheque  issued  by  the  petitioner-applicant  in  favour  of  the
respondent-complainant, totalling a sum of Rs.27,00,000/- (Rupees
Twenty Seven Lakhs).
3. Upon  trial,  the  petitioner-applicant  was  convicted  and
sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment of six months and to pay a
sum of Rs.27,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Seven Lakhs) being the value
of the cheque as compensation and in default, simple imprisonment
of two months under Section 138 of the N.I. Act by the Trial Court.
The  conviction  and  sentence  of  the  petitioner-applicant  was
affirmed by the Appellate Court as well as by the High Court of

--- Page 252 ---
2
Madras, Madurai Bench. The said order was confirmed by this Court
by order dated 26.08.2025 passed in SLP(Crl.) No.13850 of 2024.
4. The present Miscellaneous Application has been filed seeking
compounding of offence as alleged in the present case. The basis
for filing the present Miscellaneous Application is that the
petitioner-applicant is ready to discharge his entire liability of
the amount of compensation with further offer of paying some amount
beyond the said compensation as awarded by the Court below.
5. Today, the parties have left the matter to the Court for
deciding what should be the extra amount, which the petitioner-
applicant needs to pay to the respondent-complainant.
6. Since the petitioner-applicant had already deposited a sum of
Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs) before the Trial Court, from the
principal amount, a sum of Rs.17,00,000/- (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs)
is still outstanding.
7. Thus, in such view of the matter, in the considered opinion of
the Court, the ends of justice would be served, if the petitioner-
applicant pays a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs)
instead  of  Rs.17,00,000/-  (Rupees  Seventeen  Lakhs)  to  the
respondent-complainant. The same, having been accepted by the
learned counsel for the respondent, be done within four weeks from
today and shall be directly paid to the respondent-complainant.
8. Further, the respondent is entitled to withdraw the sum of
Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs), as deposited by the petitioner,
from the Trial Court, along with whatever interest, if any, which
may have accrued on the same.
9. To simplify/facilitate the matter, let the details of the bank

--- Page 253 ---
3
account of the respondent be provided by the learned counsel for
the respondent to the learned counsel for the petitioner within two
days from today.
10. Accordingly, I.A. No.291295 of 2025 along with Miscellaneous
Application stand disposed of. The order dated 26.08.2025 passed in
SLP(Crl.) No.13850 of 2024 dismissing the Special Leave Petition in
limine is recalled and the Special Leave Petition is restored to
its original file and number.
11. Leave granted.
12. For the facts and reasons recorded above and there being
compromise between the parties and as per Section 147 of the N.I.
Act providing for compounding, the Complaint Case bearing STC
No.417 of 2016 filed by the appellant against the respondent stands
compounded. The conviction and sentence of the appellant in the
said case is set aside. The appeal is allowed. 
13. We indicate that in case there is default, the present order
shall automatically stand vacated and consequences shall ensue for
the appellant.
14. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

        UPON hearing the counsel the Court made

1. Leave granted.
2. The  Appellant has  been  convicted  under
Sections 376, 417 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and
sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a
period of seven years and a fine of Rs.5,000 by
the Trial court in connection with FIR No.221 of
2012 registered at Police Station Repalle, Guntur
District,  Andhra  Pradesh.  The  conviction  was
confirmed by both the Appellate Court and the High
Court.
3. The Appellant, a II-year B. Tech student at
the time, was involved in a romantic relationship
with  the  Prosecutrix,  also  a  I-year  B.  Tech
student. It is alleged that on 29.01.2012, the
Appellant-accused  went  to  the  house  of  the
Prosecutrix, and engaged in sexual intercourse
SLP (Crl.) No.12359/2026 2/4

--- Page 265 ---
with the promise of marriage. There is another
incident spoken of, wherein a similar offence
occurred at the residence of the victim’s friend
in the month of June, 2012.
4. Learned Counsel for the Appellant submitted
that evidence of the Prosecutrix is sketchy, and
the person who is said to have seen the Appellant
enter the house of the victim on 29.01.2012, was
not examined before court. The friend, PW 3 in
whose house the second incident happened in June,
2012, though examined, didn’t speak of any such
incident having occurred. The medical report also
only spoke of a possibility of the victim having
undergone  sexual  intercourse.  Age  of  the
prosecutrix has also not been conclusively proved.
Further,  FIR  was  initially  filed  only  under
Sections 417 and 420 IPC, and Section 376 was
added later through an alteration memo.
5. On a  prima facie  consideration, we suspend
the sentence of the Appellant.
6. Appellant, if not in custody, shall appear
SLP (Crl.) No.12359/2026 3/4

--- Page 266 ---
before the Trial Court, and  if is in custody ,
shall be produced before the Trial Court and
released on bail on such conditions the Trial
Court may deem fit to impose.
7. The Registry shall call for records from the
Trial Court, and soft copy of the records shall be
supplied to the Ld. Counsels appearing for the
appellant and the State and if appearance is
recorded, of the victim.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.   2131 OF 2012  
WITH
CIVIL APPEAL NO. 2132 OF 2012
M/S GAS AUTHORITY OF INDIA LIMITED                 APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH & ORS.                  RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that
the  appellant  -  M/s.  Gas  Authority  of  India
Limited, is now known as GAIL (India) Limited and
the work of the gas supply in the Agra-Firozabad
area is now looked after by GAIL Gas Limited, a
subsidiary  of  GAIL  (India)  Limited.  The  said
statement is taken on record.
2. The  present  appeal(s)  arise  out  of  the
proceedings  of  reassessment  initiated  by  the
Deputy  Commissioner  (Assessment),  Sector  11,
Commercial Taxes, Agra, under the Entry Tax Act,
1976 for the assessment years 2004–2005 and 2005–
2006.  Show-cause  notices  were  issued  to  the
1

--- Page 292 ---
appellant for reassessment on the ground that,
subsequent  to  the  assessment  proceedings,  the
appellant has issued invoices demanding charges
for obtaining gas supply by some consumers based
on alleged tampering of meters.
3. The appellant challenged the show-cause notices
issued against them, however, during pendency of
the writ petition and the civil appeal, there are
subsequent developments, inasmuch as the consumers
against whom the appellant has raised invoices
have  initiated  arbitration  proceedings,  and  in
some of the cases, arbitration ended in awards in
favor of the consumers.
4. In view of the above, we deem it appropriate to
relegate the appellant to approach the Assessing
Officer by filing an affidavit as to the exact
status in relation to all the invoices which have
given rise to the issuance of show-cause notices
by the respondent demanding entry tax for the
assessment years 2004–2005 and 2005–2006.
5. Basing on the amount received by the appellant,
if any, against the invoices raised by it against
the consumers, the Assessing Officer who issued
the show-cause notices in the pending reassessment
proceedings shall decide the matter in accordance
with law.
6. At this stage, learned counsel for the appellant
2

--- Page 293 ---
submitted that GAIL Gas Limited, a subsidiary of
GAIL  (India)  Limited,  shall  appear  before  the
Assessing Officer. The statement is recorded.
7. The Civil Appeal(s) are disposed of in the above
terms.
8. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.         OF 2026
(arising out of SLP(Crl.) No. 13074/2026  )  
DWIPIKA BHANJO ..... APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
STATE OF ODISHA ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We see no reason to keep this appeal pending, even though
notice has not been ordered, given the fact that the impugned
order dated 22.05.2026 passed by a learned Judge of the High
Court of Orissa at Cuttack does not even relate to the case
of the appellant, Dwipika Bhanjo. The order refers to C.T.
Case No. 456/2026 arising out of Jajpur P.S. Case No. 76/2026
on  the  file  of  the  SDJM,  Jajpur,  relating  to  offences
punishable  under  Sections  316(2),  318(4),  335,  336(2),
336(3), 340, 61(2), 111 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita, 2023, read with other provisions of law, whereas the
case of the appellant is mentioned at the beginning of the
order, viz., C.T. Case No. 18(A)/2024, arising out of Khurdha
(EOW, Bhubaneswar) P.S. Case No. 08/2024 dated 28.05.2024 on
the file of the learned P.O., Designated Court under OPID
Act, Cuttack, Odisha, relating to offences punishable under
Sections 420, 467, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, read with other provisions of law. Further, the learned
1

--- Page 321 ---
Judge did not even take note of the fact that the applicants
before him were both ladies and proceeded to pass an order in
relation to a male accused.  This total non-application of
mind by the learned Judge warrants setting aside of the order
at the threshold without further ado.
3. The appeal is accordingly allowed, setting aside the impugned
order dated 22.05.2026 purportedly passed by the learned
Judge  in  BLAPL  No.  2639/2026  and  the  connected  bail
application in BLAPL No. 2637/2026 filed by Tandra Bhanjo,
the daughter of the appellant, Dwipika Bhanjo.  Both the bail
applications, that is, BLAPL No. 2637/2026 and BLAPL No.
2639/2026, which were dismissed by the impugned order, shall
stand restored to their original numbers on the file of the
High Court for adjudication afresh.  
4. In the light of the failure on the part of the High Court to
deal with the applications properly and with a modicum of
application of mind, we request the High Court to take up the
aforestated  bail  applications  immediately  and  pass
appropriate orders thereon, be it in the context of the
prayer for grant of interim relief or the main relief.
5. Pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of.
.........................J.
(SANJAY KUMAR)
.........................J.
(SANJEEV SACHDEVA)

JULY 23, 2026.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
INHERENT JURISDICTION
REVIEW PETITION (CRL.) No.313 of 2026
IN
CRIMINAL APPEAL No.1956 of 2026 
K.A. Abdul Rasheed
…Petitioner
Versus
State of Kerala                                             
…Respondent
O R D E R
The  review  is  filed  on  the  sole  ground  that  the  sentence
awarded by the Trial Court was restored, by the order in review, with
the observation that no  interference is caused because it is the
statutory  minimum  provided.  The  Trial  Court  had  convicted  the
accused  under  Section  7  &  13(1)(d)  r/w  Section  13(2)  of  the
Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 to undergo substantive sentence
of rigorous imprisonment for two years under Section 7 and three
years under Section 3(1)(d) r/w Section 13(2).
2. In fact, the offence occurred in the year 2009 and at that point
of  time  the  Prevention  of  Corruption  Act  provided  for  minimum
sentence of six months under Section 7 and one year under Section
13(2), the same having been enhanced only by Act 1 of 2014 w.e.f.
16.01.2014 vide S.O. 119 (E) dated 16th January 2014. 

--- Page 324 ---
3. The sentence maintained by us read with the observation that
no interference is caused since it is the statutory minimum is an
error on the face of the record. 
4. We were convinced that in the facts of the case the appellant
deserves only the minimum statutory sentence. Hence the review
petition  is  allowed  to  the  above  extent  and  the  appellant  is
sentenced to rigorous imprisonment of six months and a fine of
Rs.10,000/- with default sentence of simple imprisonment for three
months under Section 7 and rigorous imprisonment of one year with
Rs.10,000/- fine and default sentence of simple imprisonment for
three  months  under  Section  13(1)(d)  r/w  13(2),  to  be  run
concurrently.
5. Review Petition is allowed only to the above extent.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
.……….…….……….……. J.
                                 (SANJAY KUMAR)
.……….…….……….……. J.
                   (K. VINOD CHANDRAN)
NEW DELHI
JULY 24, 2026.

Upon hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Special Leave Petition (Crl) No. 12583 of 2026
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard the learned Senior Counsel appearing
for the appellant and the learned counsel appearing for
1

--- Page 336 ---
the respondent.
3. The appellant was charged for the offences punishable
under Sections 147, 148, 149, 302 and 307 of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860 arising out of Case Crime No.131 of
2003  registered  at  Police  Station  Kotwali,  District
Meerut, Uttar Pradesh.  Upon conviction, the appellants
were sentenced to the death penalty by the trial court.
A reference and an appeal preferred by the appellant
were made to the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
vide Criminal Reference No. 21 of 2007, whereby the High
Court, while dismissing the criminal reference, partly
allowed the appeal of the appellant and commuted the
death sentence to life imprisonment.
4. On 16.04.2026, the following order was passed in a
connected matter being S.L.P. (Crl.) No. 6745 of 2026:
“The  issue  for  consideration  in  the
present petition is as to whether the
High  Court  has  the  jurisdiction  to
sentence the petitioner to imprisonment
for life while fixing a condition that
remission  could  be  sought  only  after
completion of 20 years of sentence.
Learned  Senior  counsel  appearing
for the petitioner placed reliance upon
the judgment of this Court in  Sukhdev
Yadav @ Pehalwan  v. State of (NCT of
Delhi)  &  Ors.  –  Criminal  Appeal
No.3271/2025 dated 29th July, 2025.
Learned counsel appearing for the
State  submits  that  in  any  case,  the
petitioner having completed 21 years of
incarceration, his case for remission is
2

--- Page 337 ---
under  consideration,  and  therefore,  a
period of four weeks may be granted,
after which the present issue may be
considered.
Considering  the  above,
particularly,  the  fact  that  the
petitioner has already completed 21 years
of imprisonment, we direct  the
respondent  to  release  the  petitioner
forthwith,  until  and  unless  he  is
required in any other case, on such terms
and conditions as may be imposed by the
concerned Trial Court.
Ordered accordingly.
List the matter on 28.05.2026.”
5. In view of the above and taking into consideration
the fact that the appellant has undergone incarceration
for a period of 22 years, and the fact that the co-
accused  have  also  been  released,  the  appellant  is
directed to be released forthwith until and unless he is
required in any other case, on such terms and conditions
as may be imposed by the concerned Trial Court.
6. Accordingly, the Interlocutory Application No. 196974
of 2026 stands allowed.
7. List the Criminal Appeal in due/usual course.

--- Page 369 ---
    UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner is a foreign national (i.e., citizen of
Nepal) and is accused of an offence punishable under the
NDPS Act, 1985 for being in possession of commercial
quantity of Cocaine and Charas. In such circumstances, the
bail prayer of the petitioner was rejected by the High
Court.  Before us, a plea was raised that the petitioner
may be released on interim bail to ensure that his son, who
has an eye issue, receives proper medical treatment. 
2. The learned counsel for the respondent opposed the
prayer by submitting that if the petitioner is released, he
would abscond and being a foreign national it would be
difficult to trace him.  
3. In that backdrop, we had issued notice requiring the
State Counsel to seek instructions whether State is willing
to sponsor the medical treatment of petitioner’s son. 
4. On instructions, the learned counsel for the State
submits that the State is not willing to undertake the
expenses for the treatment of son of a foreign national who
is currently not in State’s care and custody.
5. On query, the learned counsel for the petitioner
submitted that his son who is currently in Nepal can travel
to India to All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New
2

--- Page 370 ---
Delhi for treatment, and the petitioner is not asking for
financial support but release on interim bail. 
6. Be that as it may, having regard to the nature of the
offence and the fact that petitioner is a foreign national,
we are not inclined to release the petitioner on interim
bail. More so, when his family can avail the medical
facility. Further, we do not find any error in the order of
the  High  Court  in  rejecting  the  bail  prayer  of  the
petitioner. However, we deem it appropriate to observe that
if the wife of the petitioner or any member of his family
brings the child for treatment at AIIMS, Delhi and fulfils
the necessary formalities, the facilities of consultation,
requisite surgical procedure, if necessary, etc. shall be
provided with promptitude so that the child does not
suffer.
7. With the aforesaid observations, this petition and all
pending applications shall stand disposed of.
  (KAVITA PAHUJA)                          (DIVYA BABBAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                   COURT MASTER (NSH)

ARUN @ PAVAN SHIVHARE                          Petitioner(s)

(IA No. 172777/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE

Date : 24-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing
today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Niranjan Sahu, AOR
                   Mr. Ashok Kumar Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Harashwardhan, Adv.
                                      
For Respondent(s) :Mr. Akshay Amritanshu, AOR
                   Mr. Pawanshri Aggarwal, Adv.
                   Mr. Sarthak Srivastava, Adv.
                   Mr. Nimesh Bhatt, Adv.
                                      
UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
O R D E R
1. The petitioner seeks enlargement on regular bail in
Case Crime No.03/2024 registered under Sections 419, 420,
467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC and Sections 8/20 of the
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985
(“NDPS Act”) at Police Station Girwan, District Banda.
1

--- Page 372 ---
2. The allegations are of recovery of 6 quintals and 20
Kgs of dry Ganja along with one Bolero Car and one DCM
Eicher  Truck.  There  were  five  accused  including  the
petitioner who were apprehended from the spot where the
recoveries were made. The estimated value of the seized
contraband  is  approximately  Rs.3  crores.  Notably,
chargesheet in the matter has been filed on 22.02.2024.
3. It is a matter of record that the petitioner has been
in custody since 04.01.2024 and that his co-accused have
already been enlarged on bail. It is also admitted that the
trial is yet to commence, and is now scheduled to be fixed
on 30.07.2026.
4. While it is true that the petitioner has certain
criminal antecedents, it merits observation that he was
acquitted in one of the cases under the NDPS Act, and that
he is on bail in the other case. Also, the subject offence
is said to have been committed by the petitioner by misusing
the concession of bail in the previous case.
5. There is no gainsaying that a suspect who misuses the
concession of bail by committing subsequent offences would
ordinarily not be entitled to discretionary relief. However,
we find that the present petitioner has already spent more
than eighteen months in custody. The conclusion of the trial
will also take some time.
6. Consequently, without expressing any opinion on merits,
the instant petition is disposed of and the petitioner is
directed to be released on bail subject to his furnishing
2

--- Page 373 ---
bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Special Judge. 
7. Moreover, owing to the past record of the petitioner,
he  is  directed  to  report  once  fortnightly  to  the
jurisdictional  Police  Station  for  verification  of  his
antecedents. The Trial Court shall also impose seasoned
conditions on the petitioner to ensure that he does not
misuse the concession of bail. The petitioner along with his
co-accused shall fully cooperate with the ongoing trial and
in case, he/they is/are found to have indulged in delaying
tactics, the same shall be construed to be a ground of
misuse of concession of bail and the Special Court shall be
at liberty to report the same to this Court.
8. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of with
pending application(s), if any.  
(NITIN TALREJA)                      (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                  DY. REGISTRAR

Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No. 4964/2023
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 14-10-2022
in CRLRA No. 104/2022 passed by the High Court of Gujarat at
Ahmedabad]
PINKIBEN PRAGNESHKUMAR PATEL & ANR.                Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.                        Respondent(s)
(IA No. 79549/2023 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.)
 
Date : 22-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.V.N. BHATTI
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.V. ANJARIA
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Janak V. Japee, Adv.
                   Mr. Ashutosh Ghade, AOR
                                     
For Respondent(s) :Ms. Swati Ghildiyal, AOR
                   Ms. Devyani Bhatt, Adv.
                   Ms. Annu, Adv.
                   
                   Mr. Sandeep Singh, AOR                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The Petitioners assail the order dated 14.10.2022 in Criminal
Revision Petition No. 104/2022 and pray for enhancement of the
maintenance granted by the order impugned.
3. We take note of the circumstances and the situation in which
the spouses are placed, and the precipitating circumstance, not
only  for  perpetual  litigation  but  also  for  the  claims  of
maintenance, counterclaim for maintenance, etc.

--- Page 424 ---
2
4. In our jurisdiction, we do not want to go deep into the
matter. However, we notice one infirmity in the order impugned. The
order impugned directed payment of maintenance at the rate of
Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand Only) per month from 01.01.2021.
Normally, the maintenance is directed to be paid from the date of
filing of the petition.
5. On the effective date for payment of maintenance, the learned
counsel for the respondent submits that the respondent does not
have means to pay arrears from the date of filing of the petition.
6. Means by itself is not a reason to change the effective date.
Therefore, while disposing of the Special Leave Petition, we hold
that the Petitioner No. 1 is entitled to Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five
Thousand Only) per month maintenance from 17.05.2018 and the
maintenance, as confirmed by the High Court, is not interfered with
or enhanced.
7. The Special Leave Petition is, accordingly, disposed of.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
    (LOKESH ARORA)                              (NIDHI MATHUR)
SENIOR PERSONAL ASSISTANT                     COURT MASTER (NSH)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Permission  to  file  Special  Leave  Petitions  is
granted.
2. Delay condoned.
3. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
4. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court
1

--- Page 616 ---
placed reliance on the law position as it stands under
the decision of this Court rendered by a three Judge
Bench in K. Meghachandra Singh vs. Ningam Siro , (2020) 5
SCC 689.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
correctness of the decision in  K. Meghachandra Singh
(supra)  has  been  doubted  by  a  two  Judge  Bench  in
Hariharan & Ors. vs. Harsh Vardhan Singh Rao  which is
reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1717:, 2022 (9) SCR 944.
6. Having regard to the fact that in paragraph 16 of
the High Court’s first order dated 25 th March, 2025, it
has been observed that the seniority list shall be
redrawn in case the reference is answered in favour of
the applicants, we do not find a good reason to entertain
this petition.  The  special  leave  petitions  are,
accordingly, dismissed.
7. Pending application(s), if any shall stand disposed
of.

3. However, it shall be open for the petitioner to make a

(FOR ADMISSION)
(IA No. 206095/2026 - EXEMN.FROM FILING C/C OF CERTIFICATE OF
FITNESS)
 
Date : 23-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE J.B. PARDIWALA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. VINOD CHANDRAN
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Mr. Gurinder Singh Gill, Sr. Adv.
                   Ms. Aashna Gill, AOR
                   Ms. Gagandeep, Adv.
                   Mr. Kuldeep Singh Kuchaliya, Adv.
                   Mr. P. P. Nayak, Adv.                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Exemption Application is allowed.
2. The petitioner has been denied anticipatory bail by the High
Court in connection with FIR No.178 dated 14.11.2025 registered at
PS Kulgarhi, Ferozepur , for the offence punishable under Sections
419, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (for short, ‘IPC’).
3. The Petitioner, along with others are accused of fabricating a
forged will purported to have been executed by her deceased son.

--- Page 724 ---
2
4. The complainant, daughter-in-law of the Petitioner alleges
that the will was fabricated to deprive the complainant of her
share in the properties left by her late husband. The Trial Court
and High Court rejected the Petitioner’s plea for anticipatory bail
on the ground that complicity of the Petitioner is  prime facie
established since she is the beneficiary of the Will, and the
signature  in  the  disputed  Will  did  not  match  with  admitted
signatures of the late husband of the complainant. 
4. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the other
co-accused have been released on bail, and the FIR was registered
with an inordinate delay of 4 to 5 years after the death of the
petitioner’s son. It is also submitted that the petitioner is 61
years old and extends full cooperation with the investigation and
hence, custodial interrogation is not essential.
5. In  the  facts  and  circumstances  of  the  case,  which  is
essentially a civil dispute, and when all the co-accused have been
released on bail, we are of the view that the petitioner deserves
to be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail. 
6. Therefore, we order that in the event of arrest of the
petitioner in connection with the offence enumerated above, she
shall be released on bail, subject to terms and conditions that the
Investigating Officer may deem fit to impose. 
7. Once  the  petitioner  is  released  on  bail  by  the  IO,  on
directions issued by the IO or summons issued by the jurisdictional
court, the Petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court and
furnish fresh bail bonds and ensure due appearance in the trial.
8. With the aforesaid, this petition stands disposed of.
9. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

2. The Petitioner, along with others are accused of inducing the

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
  TRANSFER PETITION(S)(CRIMINAL)  NO(S).  72/2026
RAJDIP BHUYAN                                  Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF MEGHALAYA                         Respondent(s)
O R D E R
The petitioner is seeking transfer of G.R. Case No. 36 of
2025,  which has been lodged under Sections 409 and 420 of the IPC,
pending in the Court of Ld. Judicial Magistrate , First Class, East
Jaintia Hills District, Khliehriat, Meghalaya to the Court of
competent jurisdiction at District Kamrup (Metropolitan), Guwahati.
2. The main plea raised on behalf of the petitioner is that it
was a purely commercial transaction which took place entirely at
Guwahati but a criminal complaint has been filed at East Jaintia
Hills District, Khliehriat, Meghalaya.
3. Learned  counsel  for  the  petitioner  submits  that  all
documentary evidences are available at Guwahati and not within the
territory of jurisdiction of the Magistrate, East Jaintia Hills
District, Khliehriat, Meghalaya.
4. Be that as it may, such a plea cannot be considered for
transfer of a criminal case from one Criminal Court to another
Criminal Court situated in different States.
5. The Transfer Petition, is accordingly, dismissed.
6. Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.
.......................J.
(SHREE CHANDRASHEKHAR)
NEW DELHI,
JULY 20, 2026

1

--- Page 866 ---
petitioner  against  the  order  of  conviction  and
